groups.title: Possessive-plural stem-boundary assimilation
groups.proposal: Apply the two Andrews-authorized stem-final changes only before possessive plural hu-ān.
groups.writingJob: Delete final voiceless w and assimilate final n before possessive plural hu-ān while preserving the licensed n-retaining spelling alternative.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recovering the underlying stem from the assimilated possessive-plural form.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the nounstem, subject, and possessor; the application performs the boundary change.
groups.controlPolicy: No assimilation control; the typed stem and following hu-ān determine it.

groups.title: Lexically suppletive possessive stems
groups.proposal: Use only a noun's typed Andrews-authorized possessive replacement and block invented historical forms.
groups.writingJob: Substitute an authorized possessive stem or yō-matrix, preserve person and number, support the Totēc title exception, and reject spurious totēcuiyo as a native derivation.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in connecting the possessive replacement to its source noun and in separating native grammar from historical priestly spelling.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the nounstem, subject, and possessor; lexical authority supplies the replacement stem.
groups.controlPolicy: No general suppletion control; show a genuine lexical alternative only when the source record licenses one.

groups.title: Derived nonanimate readings and possessor reduplication
groups.proposal: Keep common grammatical number on derived nonanimate predicates and apply possessor reduplication only from typed lexical authority.
groups.writingJob: Build affinity or distributive nonanimate possessive forms without converting their English plural reading into grammar number, and duplicate the typed possessor dyad only where licensed.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in separating common grammatical number, plural translation, stem relation, and repeated possessor material.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended stem relation; the application keeps number correct and applies lexically licensed reduplication.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the existing stem-meaning choice; no new general reduplication control unless an authorized lexical alternative truly remains.

groups.title: Secondary general-use relational stems
groups.proposal: Rerank a complete inner possessive predicate as a general-use stem with its authorized tē, ti, or t carrier.
groups.writingJob: Build the typed secondary general-use stem and its extended relational meanings.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the inner and outer possessive relationships.
groups.decisionSplit: Lexical authority selects the secondary stem; the user supplies the outer subject and possessor.

groups.title: Analogical tla restricted-use stems
groups.proposal: Rerank the complete tla possessive predicate as a new restricted-use stem with its general-use partner.
groups.writingJob: Build the typed analogical nounstem and preserve source coexistence or replacement as lexical information.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the rank change and resulting meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: Lexical authority licenses the derived noun; the application selects its use-stem by State.
groups.controlPolicy: Expose only a genuine lexical source-or-derived choice.

groups.title: Tl 2-A reclassification and possessor scope
groups.proposal: Reclassify an authorized tl 2-A source as tl 1-A and keep the NNC-internal possessor nuclear.
groups.writingJob: Delete the ephemeral i, rebuild connectors for tl 1-A, and preserve nuclear versus supplementary possessor scope.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through reclassification, meaning alternatives, and possessor rank.
groups.decisionSplit: Lexical authority licenses reclassification; the application performs it.
groups.controlPolicy: No mechanical reclassification control for arbitrary input.

groups.title: Naturally possessed and never-possessive nounstems
groups.proposal: Enforce lexical State availability for property, relationship, body-part, and never-possessive stems.
groups.writingJob: Require possessive State where natural association demands it and permit an explicit metaphorical override where Andrews licenses one.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through possession scope and English singular or plural interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended meaning; lexical policy allows or blocks State.
groups.controlPolicy: No natural-possession toggle; use lexical authority and expose metaphorical use only when meaningful.

groups.title: NNCs as complete sentences
groups.proposal: Send the finished typed NNC through sentence grammar for statement, question, exclamation, polarity, mood, and particles.
groups.writingJob: Build the normal sentence from the canonical NNC without inventing a have verb or encoding definiteness in the predicate.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through equative, attributive, adverbial, having, and definite or indefinite translations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses genuine sentence meaning; the application supplies structure and punctuation.
